title: Zero-Trust Audit & Approval Gates — Private Deployments PRD (draft)
content:
Status: draft — working PRD for scoping audit telemetry and approval flows for Private deployments.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers deploying Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) require clear, auditable events for operator actions plus an operator approval workflow for sensitive config changes (networking, KMS, model pinning).
- Current hosted audit surface is insufficient for private environments where customers demand fine-grained control, long-term retention, and exportability to their SIEM.
- Some regulated customers require an approval gate that is enforced by the control plane (not only via process) prior to applying network or IAM changes.

Goals:
- Define an audit-event schema and minimum retention/export capabilities for Private.
- Design an approval-gates system that integrates with customer-managed identity and RBAC, supports delegated approvals, and records evidence for compliance.
- Provide clear deployment/networking patterns that work for cloud VPCs and on-prem air-gapped installs (connectors, proxies, or direct peering).
- Minimize operator friction: UX for operators and automated policies for typical changes.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not specify the full offline forensic pipeline (long-term cold storage architectures) — we'll tie into customer export requirements in a follow-up.
- We are not building a generic workflow engine; approval flows are limited-scope for security-relevant operations.

Primary stakeholders:
- Product: Maya Torres (lead)
- Eng: Rajat Singh (backend), Diego Alvarez (networking), Liam O'Neal (control plane)
- Security & Compliance: Hannah Kim
- Solutions/SE: (feedback loop during alpha)

Key user stories:
1) As a security engineer at AcmeBank, I want every config change that affects network egress and KMS usage to create an immutable audit event and require 2-person approval before it reaches production.
2) As a platform operator, I want the ability to export audit streams to CloudWatch/Splunk/Seq via a customer-configured forwarder.
3) As an admin, I want to delegate approvers (team A can approve dev changes, team B must approve prod changes) and see the approval history in the console and the audit feed.

Functional requirements (high level):
- Audit event model: every state-changing API (create/update/delete) in the Private control plane emits a structured audit event with: actor (user/service), actor_id, act_source (console/api/automation), action_type, resource_type, resource_id, before_state (optional), after_state (optional), timestamp, trace_id, request_id, approval_token (if change is gated), outcome (pending/approved/rejected).
- Retention & export: per-customer retention policy (default 90d), with ability to configure automatic export to: S3, CloudWatch, Splunk HEC, or syslog endpoint; support for streaming export and batch export.
- Approval gates: configurable per-resource-type and per-environment (dev/staging/prod). Gate types: manual approval (1..N approvers), automated policy (e.g., require KMS key rotation less than X), and out-of-band webhook callback for third-party approvers.
- RBAC tie-in: approvals should respect customer SSO groups/roles; support for OIDC groups, SCIM provisioning hints, and native role mappings in the control plane.
- UI/UX: console shows pending approvals, requester info, diff view of change, and audit link. Approvers can accept/reject with comments.
- Automation hooks: REST API to create/authorize/complete approvals, webhook callbacks on decision, and programmatic grants for automation principals.

Non-functional requirements:
- Tamper-resistance: once written, audit events must be append-only and signed (HMAC or customer-managed key if requested).
- SLA: approval workflow responses should be delivered within 1s for UI actions and within 5s for webhook acknowledgements (best-effort for private + on-prem topologies).
- Performance: emitting audit events should not add >50ms p50 latency to control-plane calls.
- Scale: support up to 10k audit events/day/customer for large enterprise; elastic for hosted control plane that manages many private instances.

Audit event schema (proposal example):
- event_type: "config.change"
- timestamp: "2026-02-28T14:12:08Z"
- actor: "ava.chen@redwood.com"
- actor_id: "user-34219"
- source: "console"
- action: "update_network_policy"
- resource: "vpc-connector-9"
- resource_type: "vpc_connector"
- before: "{masked/local-only summary}"
- after: "{masked/local-only summary}"
- approval: "pending|approved|rejected"
- approval_token: "appr-8f3a"
- trace_id: "trace-..."
(Implementation note: before/after can be optional or replaced by a delta object to avoid full config leakage; we need to consult security about PII in diffs.)

Retention & export details:
- Default retention: 90 days; enterprise option: 7 years (export recommended).
- Export formats: newline-delimited JSON (ndjson), optional compression (gzip).
- Delivery guarantees: at-least-once delivery for forwarders; sequence-numbered batches for compatibility with SIEM deduplication.
- Customer-managed key option: signed blobs with customer KMS for attestability.

Approval gates flow (happy path):
1) Operator submits change via console/API. Control plane creates draft change, emits audit event with approval:pending and assigns approval_token.
2) If policy matches gate (e.g., network change in prod), create approval workflow and notify approvers (console, email, webhook).
3) Approver inspects diff, optionally requests clarification (comment -> audit event).
4) Approver approves -> control plane validates approver identity and marks approval token as approved; emit audit event: outcome=approved; apply change.
5) If rejected, emit outcome=rejected and rollback draft.

RBAC & delegation model (sketch):
- Roles: viewer, operator, approver, emergency-operator.
- Mapping: customer SSO group X -> approver for env=dev; SSO group Y -> approver for env=prod.
- Emergency bypass: emergency-operator role can approve with 2 factor and an automated post-hoc review (logged and flagged for SOC).

Customer-managed networking implications:
- Supported patterns:
  - In-cloud VPC peering / AWS Transit Gateway with firewall rules configured by customer.
  - PrivateLink/Private Endpoint models for AWS/GCP equivalents for zero public ingress.
  - On-prem connector (outbound-only tunnel) that maintains a persistent control channel; all control-plane actions go through this channel in air-gapped installs.
- Requirements by pattern:
  - Peering: need clear guidance for routing, DNS, and CIDR allocation; audit events must include the peering-id and routing-change details.
  - PrivateLink: must surface endpoint IDs and certificate thumbprints in audit events.
  - Connector: ensure the connector SDK can forward audit events locally and buffer for export if connectivity drops.

UX & developer experience notes:
- Console: simple toggle to "Require approvals for: network, kms, model-pinning" with per-environment scoping.
- APIs: provide a small SDK for programmatic approvals (useful for infra-as-code pipelines).
- Notifications: integration with Slack and Teams via webhooks for approver mentions.

Compliance mapping (initial):
- SOC2: audit trail, access controls, change-approval evidence.
- HIPAA/Phi: ensure diffs are redacted if they contain PII; require BAA for export to third-party.
- GDPR: support data export and deletion requests for user-identified fields in audit logs (minimize PII stored).

Rollout plan (phased):
- Alpha (private customers + internal): enable audit stream + basic manual approvals; collect feedback on diff formats and retention. Target: 8 customers. (Q2 2026)
- Beta: add export connectors (S3, Splunk), RBAC integration with major SSO providers. Target: 30 customers. (Q3 2026)
- GA: signed audit blobs, emergency-bypass controls, full console UX, SLAs. (Q4 2026)

Open questions / risks:
- How to securely store "before" and "after" without retaining sensitive values? (masked diffs vs pointers to customer-owned blob store).
- Approval enforcement boundary for on-prem connector: will customers accept control-plane-enforced approvals if control messages route through their connector? Need legal/product alignment.
- Export latency requirements for customers who want near-real-time SIEM ingestion.
- Cross-account approval trust: customers with multi-account setups want approvers from central account; how to federate?

Next steps / immediate action items:
- [ ] Engineering: prototype append-only audit store with ndjson export and small schema (Rajat, due 2026-03-15).
- [ ] Product: finalize gate types and UI wireframes (Maya, due 2026-03-01).
- [ ] Security: review diff redaction policy and KMS signing options (Hannah, due 2026-03-10).
- [ ] Solutions: prepare checklist for early adopter customers (Diego, due 2026-03-08).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally focused on high-sensitivity resources (network, KMS, model pinning). Lower-sensitivity changes (logs-level, tagging) should default to audit-only and not gate.
- Feedback needed: preferred default retention, acceptance by SREs for signing approach, and feasibility of emergency-bypass audit workflows.

Historical context / related work:
- Builds on hosted control-plane audit primitives (team: eng-observability) but must expand for private connectivity topologies.
- See CON-3452 for prior compliance mappings and the linked prototype PR for ndjson export.

End of draft.

(Notes: rough draft, expect incomplete UX details, heavy engineering input required. Document will be iterated with SEs during alpha.)
